findings.description: The `gate_patterns` for `σ_measured` includes `r"sigma[_\s]*measured"` which uses `\s*` (zero or more whitespace chars). In Python regex, `\s` matches `[\t\n\r\f\v ]` — including newlines. Combined with the unanchored `re.search` on the multi-line `block` text, this pattern can match across line boundaries. If the block contains the word "sigma" on one line and "measured" on the next (or separated by any whitespace including newlines), the pattern matches and the subsequent `\s*[:\-=]?\s*(PASS|FAIL|N/A|NA)` captures status from wherever PASS/FAIL appears after that cross-line match. This produces false status attribution: a PASS/FAIL token on a line unrelated to σ_measured gets captured as its status.

findings.description: The function's return type `List[str]` loses the distinction between three semantically different gate states: (1) gate explicitly PASS, (2) gate is σ_measured with N/A status, (3) gate not mentioned at all. States (1) and (2) both result in the gate being ABSENT from the returned list. State (3) results in the gate being PRESENT in the list (same as explicit FAIL). The caller — specifically the feedback channel dispatcher in `_feedback.py` — cannot distinguish "σ_measured was verified and passed" from "σ_measured was declared N/A" after this function returns. This blocks the feedback channel from implementing C0016's fix (contextual N/A validation) at the caller level.

## SCHEMA FEEDBACK RESPONSE

**CC2_F005**: WITHDRAW. The finding is a near-duplicate of Gemini_F005 (cosine 0.78) and lacks the required ADMISSIBILITY block. Withdrawn per §17.

---

## VERDICTS ON EXISTING FINDINGS

**CONFIRM C0014** — The `marker_match` regex ending with `\s*$` fails when trailing content follows on the same line (e.g., `ADMISSIBILITY: (per §15)`). The `$` in MULTILINE mode requires end-of-line, so any inline trailing text after the optional parenthetical blocks the match. Verified by tracing the regex: `(?:\([^)]*\))?` handles one parenthetical, but text AFTER it (or a non-parenthetical suffix) causes `\s*$` to fail.

**CONFIRM C0016** — `σ_measured: N/A` is accepted unconditionally. The parser treats N/A as equivalent to PASS regardless of whether a FIX section exists in the finding. Per §15, N/A is only valid when no fix is proposed and no post-fix measurement is applicable. The code has no fix-presence check.

**CONFIRM C0033** — Empty `finding_text` returns all 5 gates via `if not finding_text: return list(ADMISSIBILITY_GATES)`. This is semantically confusing — an empty string is not the same as a missing ADMISSIBILITY block, yet both produce identical output.

**EXTEND C0029** | The section_terminator's brittleness extends to markdown-formatted subsequent headers. The marker regex handles markdown via `(?:#{1,6}\s*)?`, but the terminator uses bare `^\s*(KEYWORD)\s*:` with no markdown prefix allowance. If the next section is `## NOVELTY:` or `### VERIFIED:`, the terminator fails — `^\s*` matches, then expects a keyword but encounters `#`. Consequence: the ADMISSIBILITY block consumes the entire remainder of the finding text, parsing gate statuses from unrelated sections. This is a concrete additional edge case beyond the missing-ADMISSIBILITY-header and parenthetical issues C0029 already names.

---

FINDING_ID: F006
SEVERITY: 0.65
FLAW_CLASS: 5

FIND: The `gate_patterns` for `σ_measured` includes `r"sigma[_\s]*measured"` which uses `\s*` (zero or more whitespace chars). In Python regex, `\s` matches `[\t\n\r\f\v ]` — including newlines. Combined with the unanchored `re.search` on the multi-line `block` text, this pattern can match across line boundaries. If the block contains the word "sigma" on one line and "measured" on the next (or separated by any whitespace including newlines), the pattern matches and the subsequent `\s*[:\-=]?\s*(PASS|FAIL|N/A|NA)` captures status from wherever PASS/FAIL appears after that cross-line match.
